If filter is not provided, the count of all points in the collection will be returned.' — the assertion is a faithful paraphrase; note the doc promises filter-generic exact counting (membership semantics for has_id via the Filter schema), and promises no per-condition count arithmetic beyond that. http_semantics.note: The F6 request is a well-formed, fully valid request (legal filter, exact=true boolean); no client-side-decidable error is involved, so the 2xx-vs-4xx question does not apply. The 200 response with count=4 is the documented success shape.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: exact=true (default) performs an exact count (slower); an omitted filter counts all points
contract_grounding.note: violates=False is the genuinely-compliant branch of the self-check, not the vague middle: the observed count 4 IS the exact number of points matching the filter — the seeded collection contains ids 1..12 (baseline count==12 in the same log), so has_id [1,2,3,9] matches exactly {1,2,3,9} = 4 points, and id 9's existence is independently proven by F2 (paris==4, paris ids are 9..12 by the script's own construction). The 3-vs-4 mismatch is against the script's mis-derived oracle, not against the assertion's promise. Also note: candidates.jsonl's constraint_id field is empty; the constraint id was recovered from the attack string and the script header '# constraint_ids: qdrant_behavioral_points_count_001', and the assertion exists verbatim in structured_contract.json assertions[] (evidence_tier explicit, level endpoint).

script: raw request face correct (POST /collections/{coll}/points/count, body {"filter":{"must":[{"has_id":[1,2,3,9]}]},"exact":true}, fresh uuid-tagged collection, wait=true upsert, baseline anchor 12 OK) — BUT the F6 oracle expectation 3 contradicts the script's own arrange step: seed loop range(1,13) makes id 9 an existing paris point, so the correct arithmetic-derived expectation is 4; the docstring's own 'R33 lesson: id-collision analysis' was violated by including in-range id 9 — oracle link broken

log: the DEFECT_FOUND (Type4) verdict line is the mechanical product of the mis-derived expectation (got 4 != expected 3); the raw response count=4 is arithmetically correct for the seeded set, so the verdict does not evidence a target-side state-logic violation — log link inherits the script break
chain_trace.break_detail: The break is in the script's expected-value derivation, not in the request construction and not in the target's behavior: line 159 sets expected=3 for has_id [1,2,3,9] while lines 178-180 seed ids 1..12 (id 9 = paris). The filter's true matching set is {1,2,3,9} (all four exist, proven by baseline==12 and F2 paris==4 within the same log), so exact=true returning 4 satisfies the assertion 'exact=true returns the exact number of points matching the filter'. The log's Type4 verdict is a false positive caused by the oracle arithmetic error (apparent intent: include one non-existent id to prove has_id does not over-count — that requires an id outside 1..12, e.g. 13 or 99).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST POST /collections/{name}/points/count -> Collection::count (point_ops.rs:407; fans out per shard and sums counts) -> LocalShard::count (shard_ops.rs:347; exact branch at :365 runs read_filtered over the filter and takes all_points.len(), approximate branch uses estimate_cardinality) -> SegmentsSearcher::read_filtered (segments_searcher.rs:420; materializes the matching external point ids into a deduplicating BTreeSet across segments) -> per-segment read_filtered -> check_payload (query_checker.rs:116), where Condition::HasId is evaluated as plain set membership of the point's external id (has_id.has_id.contains(&id)). HasIdCondition itself is defined at types.rs:3279. Net semantics: exact=true returns |matching external ids|; for a collection holding ids 1..12 and filter has_id [1,2,3,9] the code must and does return 4.
source_grounding.note: The behavior the constraint requires (exact=true -> exact, filter-aware count) is present and correctly implemented in source: exact counts are computed by materializing the matching id set, and has_id is membership semantics. Source therefore corroborates count=4 as the correct exact count for this request; nothing in the source suggests an alternative (e.g. filter-ignoring or approximate) path was taken with exact=true.
